problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=-2v+1,\,y=4u-v-5.
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]$
- $det(A)=-4$
- The transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving

examples.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $\mathbf T$ defined as

$$
x = v - u-6, \qquad y = v -2u  .
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $\mathbf T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/af7ea1dee03533df623aef652cc2eb8cc7590647ef10652163e14d3a322f7b7f.png)

- $\det(A) = 1$

- The transformation $\mathbf T$ is orientation-preserving
examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is true. Indeed, notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-u-6 \\ v-2u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u+v \\ -2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $\mathbf T$ is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/6522a8eb76f3ff239aefdd3c7aff95ddfedbc5deb8be854002643afba4b94411.png)

- Statement II is true. Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/aadc5c7a23fd39c8329d35a3b9befdd0eb48b2e97e4122744d1a4e19e0ce45d6.png)

- Statement III is true. Indeed, since $\det(A) > 0,$ the affine transformation $\mathbf T$ is orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/be30ef880c451fec095190537577b09896aa6b849e99b90f8185501ee0ef1296.png)

Consider the rectangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=u+v,\,y=u-v-1.
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ u-v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/06ceacb05656e99e545561e5cd5733529a1cf7f052beb6086b2fd42667041713.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-1,-2),(1,0),(2,-1),$ and $(0,-3).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/92b9079151925202a5346e6b1dd2082b21a4e4102720673773e958c5f3644c4f.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-2<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.
